name: Kernel

modes.label: Headless
modes.note: One GB active browser runtime; idle standby free.

modes.label: Headful (8 or 16 GiB)
modes.note: Headful Chromium with Live View + computer controls API; $0.0000166667/GB-second: 8 GiB default ($0.48/h), 16 GiB when `memory` is set on create ($0.96/h). No guaranteed CPU count.

modes.label: Headful GPU
modes.note: Start-Up+ only; USD 0.0008000016/s (48x the GB-second rate); no standby (billed until deleted); us-east only; not available in browser pools. GPU model unpublished.

modes.label: App invocation (serverless agent code, 4 GB)
modes.note: USD 0.0000666668/s = USD 0.24/h at 4 GB; billed only while code runs; browsers billed separately; invocation concurrency 5/10/50 (20 per app on Start-Up).

plans.name: Start-Up
plans.note: GPU, regional browsers and BYO proxy; 30-day replays. App concurrency 50 org / 20 per app. Free trial offered (length not published); priority email support; browser pools, unlimited custom extensions/projects, audit log export.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: SSO, HIPAA BAA, dedicated support, ZDR, custom limits.

features.ip_note: Direct egress by default; Kernel-provided datacenter, ISP, residential and mobile proxies are unmetered (fair use); stealth mode adds a static ISP proxy + CAPTCHA solver; BYO proxy on Start-Up/Enterprise.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
The homepage GB-second rate and docs preset rates agree: 1 GB headless, 8 GB headful. 16 GB is a documented headful option. Do not charge CPU+RAM again on top.
Standby billing is based on browser activity, not CPU utilization. An open active live view/CDP workload may prevent savings. Pool and standby browsers continue consuming concurrency.
Pool availability conflicts internally: feature table says all tiers; FAQ says Start-Up and Enterprise. Fifty-browser example already needs Start-Up.
Idle pool disks are free, but snapshot_gib_month stays null because general snapshot storage is not priced. Browser profiles are not general disks.

Headful = Chromium on a virtual display with Live View and a computer-controls API, not a full desktop environment; SSH into the browser VM is available (kernel browsers ssh). Headless has no Live View.

eu-west / ap-southeast browsers need the Start-Up or Enterprise plan. On Free and Hobbyist Kernel is US-only (us-east), so an EU/Asia workload must pay the USD 200 Start-Up plan. Model this as region-specific mode copies with plans:["Start-Up","Enterprise"], or as a plan gate.
16 GiB headful price (USD 0.96/h) is derived from the GB-second definition; the docs pricing table lists only one headful rate (USD 0.0001333336/s = 8 GB).
YC startups get a discount ('here's our yc deal'). Terms are behind a link and not published on the pricing page.

knobs.label: Fraction outside standby
knobs.why: Standby begins after 5 seconds without CDP/live-view activity, not at low CPU use.

fleet.notes: Quota is org-wide and includes reserved browser-pool capacity and standby browsers, even idle/unacquired. 10 fits Hobbyist, 50 Start-Up, 300/1,000 Enterprise. App invocation concurrency is separate. Per-project concurrency caps (org default + per-project override) sit under the org cap. API requests are rate-limited per organization (HTTP 429 + Retry-After); the numeric limit is unpublished and raised via contact.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: One of the most powerful features of our approach is the ability to create complete snapshots of the browser's state when entering standby mode. These snapshots capture everything:
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: standby after 5 s with no CDP/WebDriver/Live View/computer-controls activity ('Kernel browsers automatically enter standby after `five seconds` with no activity', /docs/browsers/standby). Memory included: list includes 'Loaded page content and DOM state' and 'Active downloads and processes'; restored 'in milliseconds' on next connection. Limits: the standby browser is still deleted after its timeout (default 60 s, max 72 h) counted from standby, so the snapshot does not outlive the session; 'GPU-accelerated browsers do not support standby mode.'

snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint/fork endpoint in the full OpenAPI spec or docs. Closest: browser profiles (cookies/storage/browser state) that are saved when a browser with save_changes is deleted or times out ('When the Kernel browser is deleted or times out, Kernel replaces the stored profile with that browser's complete state.') and loaded by new browsers - browser state only, not a machine/memory snapshot. Browser pools keep pre-warmed browsers.

harness_api.note: No endpoints to start/stream/resume Claude Code, Codex or a Kernel agent inside the browser VM. Kernel apps (deploy/invoke/invocation events) run your own code; process exec/spawn is a generic exec API; Managed Auth is a narrow login agent; Claude Code integration is Kernel as an MCP server/skills used FROM Claude Code, not a harness inside Kernel.

ingress_rules.note: Browser VMs expose no arbitrary public ports; access is only via per-session tokenized CDP/WebDriver/Live View URLs (Live View can be read-only) and API-authenticated 'kernel browsers ssh' with -L/-R port forwarding. No IP allowlists or user-chosen public port URLs. Network-access page: 'You don't need to open inbound ports.'

secret_proxy.quote: fill isn't secret isolation from the browser. an agent with unrestricted browser access, page scripts, or extensions can read values after filling.
secret_proxy.note: Vault 'fill' writes credentials into browser form fields (values enter the VM, hidden only from your app/model context); Managed Auth logs in and stores cookies in a profile; app secrets are env vars. Exception, payments only: agentcard integration gives the agent non-secret card aliases and Kernel intercepts the recognized checkout request at egress ('the card number and cvc stay with agentcard. your agent receives non-secret aliases.') - a true out-of-VM substitution but limited to card checkout formats, not arbitrary HTTP credentials. No coverage of DB/SSH/git.

volume_attach.note: No volume/disk resources in the API; storage is the ephemeral browser VM filesystem (File I/O API upload/download) plus browser profiles and extensions.

volume_shared.quote: Each browser session loads its own profile snapshot. Profiles don't synchronize changes between running browsers
volume_shared.note: One profile can be attached to many browsers but as a per-browser copy, not a live shared filesystem; no shared volumes.
